subject: Marketplace listing: latency-aware fallback & canary slicing plan
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Amy Chen <amy@nimbusanalytics.com>, Azure Marketplace Ops <mp-ops@azuremarketplace.com>, AWS Partner <aws-partner@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace listing: latency-aware fallback & canary slicing plan

Team / partners —

I wanted to circulate a working proposal for how we surface SKUs and fallback variants across AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace listings, with a pragmatic canary plan focused on latency-sensitive regions. Goal: avoid a one-size-fits-all SKU that either blows up latency or drives up unit cost for small customers.

High-level idea:
- SKU tiers: Core (low-cost, quantized/8-bit), Standard (default), Enterprise (full-precision, priority routing).
- Marketplace listing flags: each cloud listing will advertise the SKU family and a "fallback variant" (lower-cost runtime) we can route to when latency SLOs are threatened.
- Latency-aware fallback: per-region p95 thresholds — if p95 > 250ms for Standard, route new requests to Core variant for non-enterprise entitlements.
- Canary slicing: start APAC canary at 5% traffic for 48h, ramp to 20% over two weeks if error/latency stays within SLOs. For EU/US we want a separate canary window tied to local usage patterns.

Questions / asks:
1) Ben — can you attach the latest per-region latency profiles and call out realistic p95 thresholds for each cloud?
2) Amy / Nimbus — do you have customers who require single-cloud commitments (i.e., cannot accept our fallback to a different backend variant)?
3) Marketplace ops — any constraints from Azure / AWS listing metadata (flags/attributes) we need to include to support runtime-routing?

I've attached a draft SKU matrix (sku_matrix_q4.xlsx) with proposed names and short descriptions. Please reply with comments — I propose a 30-minute sync Monday to lock names and the APAC canary window.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Head of Partner GTM
Redwood Inference
[attachment: sku_matrix_q4.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Chen <amy@nimbusanalytics.com>, Azure Marketplace Ops <mp-ops@azuremarketplace.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing: latency-aware fallback & canary slicing plan

Mina — thanks for this clear framing. Quick notes from infra/load perspective:

- I attached the observed latency profiles for the three clouds (latency-profiles.csv). Short summary: GCP appears ~10-15% faster median for our Standard serving images in US-West; Azure shows more variance in APAC during evening windows.
- Suggested p95 thresholds: US/EU: 200ms for Standard, 300ms for Core when used as fallback; APAC: 250ms for Standard. We should be conservative for initial canary.
- Routing implications: implementing routing based on observed p95 requires a short (60s) sampling window and a hysteresis (5% traffic floor) to avoid oscillation.

One question on entitlements: how do we enforce "Enterprise only" routing in marketplace-configured offers? If the marketplace listing cannot express entitlements granularly, we need to handle enforcement at runtime (token scope) and ensure the listing copy is explicit.

Ben
Principal Reliability Eng — Redwood Inference
[attachment: latency-profiles.csv (csv)]

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing: latency-aware fallback & canary slicing plan

Thanks Mina — this looks promising. A couple items from Nimbus side:

- Our EU customers are 42% of total traffic and are sensitive to latency spikes; we prefer Standard/Enterprise routing in EU where possible. APAC is growing for us — happy to take part in an APAC canary.
- We do have a few regulated customers (healthcare) that require explicit single-cloud contracts for data residency; for those customers we cannot accept a fallback to a different runtime that changes residency. Those will need to be marked Enterprise and excluded from automatic fallback.
- Timeline question: what is the certification path for Azure listing metadata? Our marketplace team needs ~3 weeks lead time to coordinate co-sell asset creation.

Also happy to join the Monday sync — my availability: Mon 11/16 10:00–11:30 PT.

Best,
Amy Chen
Head of Platform Ops, Nimbus Analytics
amy@nimbusanalytics.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Azure Marketplace Ops <mp-ops@azuremarketplace.com>, Amy Chen <amy@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing: latency-aware fallback & canary slicing plan

This all looks good. A few operational proposals from GTM / listings side:

- Canary gating: APAC first (5% for 48h -> 10% for 72h -> 20% over 2 weeks). EU/US canary windows should be separate and aligned to local peak hours (EU: 06:00–12:00 UTC for our customers).
- Entitlement enforcement: use marketplace SKUs + token-scoped enforcement. Listing copy must clearly state fallback behavior. For regulated Nimbus customers, mark them as "enterprise: geo-locked" in our entitlement service.
- Listing metadata: Azure allows custom tags on offers (we can surface sku_family and fallback_enabled). AWS allows a free-form attribute in the offer description but requires co-sell manifest updates for marketplace sales — will need a short doc from marketplace ops.

Next steps (owner):
- Ben: finalize p95 thresholds and confirm sampling window / hysteresis (owner: Ben)
- Mina: finalize SKU names and marketplace copy (owner: Mina)
- Marketplace Ops: share publication constraints & timeline for Azure/AWS (owner: mp-ops)
- Amy: confirm regulated customer list for geo-locking (owner: Amy)

Propose we lock copy + canary schedule on Monday 11/16. I'm adding the HubSpot deal link to the thread for tracking: https://hubspot.com/deals/DEAL-8791

—Lauren
Director, GTM Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing: latency-aware fallback & canary slicing plan

Thanks everyone — solid alignment. Quick confirmation and actions:

- Ben: please run a short 48h simulated load against the Standard images in APAC next week and validate p95 < 250ms target with the 60s sampling window + 5% hysteresis. Share results by EOD Tue.
- Lauren: I'll draft the marketplace copy and SKU naming convention by Monday morning and share a one-page for review.
- Azure / AWS ops: please share any hard constraints on metadata fields or co-sell manifest timing — we want to ensure the canary window doesn't miss publication lead-time.
- Amy: please send the list of regulated customers (email a short CSV) so we can set geo-locked entitlements before the canary.

I'll set the Monday 11/16 10:30 PT sync and share a calendar invite. Attaching the SKU matrix and latency profile again for visibility.

Mina
